commit.message:
[Fetch] Don't report a completed fetch() body as cancelled

DevTools got Network.loadingFailed with net::ERR_ABORTED and
canceled: true instead of Network.loadingFinished, and lost the
response body, for fetch() responses whose body had been fully
received:
- a Cache-Control: no-store body read to the end with
  response.body.getReader(), when the end of the body arrived
  separately from the last data chunk;
- an empty body that the page never read.

When the end of the body was signalled in its own OnStateChange(),
ResponseBodyLoader's DelegatingBytesConsumer notified its client before
recording the done state. BodyStreamBuffer saw the closed state, closed
the stream and cancelled the consumer, which was still loading, so the
load ended in ResourceLoader::Cancel(). BodyStreamBuffer is the direct
client of a no-store body, which FetchManager does not buffer. Other
bodies go through a BufferingBytesConsumer, which until it starts
buffering after a delay forwards the notification and, with nothing
buffered, the closed state. An errored body was reported as cancelled
the same way.

Record the terminal result before notifying the client, as BeginRead()
already does, so that the client's cancellation is a no-op and the load
finishes or fails as it should.

Bug: 568852319, 371021302

@@ -0,0 +1,12 @@
+Tests that fetch() requests whose body has been received finish loading.
+
+Scenario 1: No-store body read to the end with a stream reader
+Page: Hello world
+Event: Network.loadingFinished
+Body: 'Hello world'
+
+Scenario 2: Empty body that is never read
+Page: 200
+Event: Network.loadingFinished
+Body: ''
+
